content.text:
**`entire session list` calls no Entire APIs at all — it's a purely local, filesystem-only command.**

## The command path

`cmd/entire/cli/sessions.go:346` `runSessionList` does exactly one thing:

```
runSessionList
  └─ strategy.ListSessionStates(ctx)        session_state.go:144
       └─ session.NewStateStore(ctx)         state.go:558  → <git-common-dir>/entire-sessions/
            └─ StateStore.List(ctx)          state.go: os.ReadDir + per-file Load
```

`StateStore.List` reads `*.json` files out of `.git/entire-sessions/` (git common dir, so it's shared across worktrees), unmarshals each one, drops corrupted/stale entries, and returns them. Sorting, the card rendering, and `--json` (`writeSessionListJSON`) all operate on that in-memory slice. No control-plane client, no cell client, no git network operation — not even a shadow-branch read.

## What does go over the network

Two things fire from the root command's `PersistentPostRun` (`root.go:65`) after *any* non-hidden command, `session list` included:

| Call | Endpoint | Condition |
|---|---|---|
| Version check | `GET https://api.github.com/repos/entireio/cli/releases/latest` (and `/releases?per_page=20`) — `versioncheck/types.go:19` | Always, 2s timeout, cached in `~/.cache/entire/version_check.json`, notice to stderr |
| Telemetry | PostHog `https://eu.i.posthog.com` — `telemetry/detached.go:23` | Only when `telemetry: true` in settings; detached subprocess, non-blocking |

Neither is part of the listing — both are ambient CLI behavior, and neither touches an Entire host.

For contrast: sibling session commands *do* hit the API. `entire session info --transcript` and the activity/recap paths use `auth.NewEntireAPICellClient` (home-cell routing via the `home_jurisdiction` claim), and `entire activity` falls back to the data API. `list` deliberately stays local, which is why it works offline and without auth.

Description:
Problem:
The entire agent add, entire agent remove, and entire agent list commands did not discover external agent plugins (binaries on $PATH named entire-<agent-name>). Users could enable external agents with entire enable --agent <name>, but then couldn't manage them with the agent commands, breaking the expectation that agent management tools work consistently.
Solution:
Added external agent discovery to the agent management commands:
entire agent list now calls DiscoverAndRegisterAlways() before listing, so external agents appear in the output alongside built-in agents
entire agent add <name> now resolves the named external agent before registering it, executing only that specific binary rather than scanning all of $PATH
entire agent remove <name> similarly resolves the named external agent before removal
This makes agent discovery consistent across enable, add, remove, and list commands. The discovery bypasses the external_agents setting gate since these commands are themselves the explicit opt-in for agent management. Added a test to verify external agents appear in the listing.

# Review: Trail #992 — `fix: agent add/list/remove now discover external agents`

**Branch:** `fix/1928-agent-group-external-discovery` → `main` · 6 commits · +142/−10 across 3 files · author gtrrz-victor

I checked out the branch, built it against `main`, and exercised the paths with mock plugins rather than only reading the diff.

**Verification status:** `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/...` all green · `golangci-lint` 0 issues · `gofmt` clean.

## Verdict

The core fix is correct and well-designed. The targeted-by-name discovery in `add`/`remove` is the right call — I confirmed `entire agent add claude-code` triggers **zero** plugin executions (the `agent.Get` short-circuit at `discovery.go:97` fires before any `$PATH` lookup), so built-ins are untouched. Unknown names still route to `printWrongAgentError` with exit 1, errors go to stderr, and a broken plugin now yields a real diagnostic instead of "unknown agent" — exactly the stated goal. `agent add <external>` auto-enables `external_agents` via `setup.go:1926`, so the invariant the `runAgentList` comment relies on genuinely holds.

Two things I'd want addressed before merge, neither a blocker on correctness.

## 1. Default `agent list` now executes every plugin twice — and may display none of them

`runAgentList` calls gated `DiscoverAndRegister` even in the default path, then *filters uninstalled externals out of the display*. So the `--all` split is display-only; it does not reduce execution. Each plugin is run twice: `info` during discovery, `are-hooks-installed` via `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled`.

Measured, `agent list` on `main` vs this branch with `external_agents: true`:

| Plugins on PATH | main | branch |
|---|---|---|
| 2 compiled Go plugins | 0.087s | 0.094s |
| 1 Python plugin | 0.084s | **0.205s** |
| 9 shell-script plugins | 0.05s / 0 execs | **1.72s / 18 execs** |

In the 9-plugin case I diffed the output: **byte-identical to main's**, because none were installed. The cost scales with plugin count × startup latency, so compiled plugins are fine and interpreted ones (a plausible way to write an agent integration) are not.

I'd flag this as *worth a look* rather than a regression — gated `DiscoverAndRegister` is already on `hooks_cmd`, `resume`, `attach`, `explain`, and `review`. But those aren't a sub-100ms listing command. The cheapest fix that keeps commit 896e533fe's intent (installed externals visible by default) is to persist installed external names at `agent add` time and have the default path call `DiscoverAndRegisterNamedAlways` per known name. There's no such record today — I checked `EntireSettings`, and `AreHooksInstalled` is the only source of truth — so this is a design question for the author, not a one-line change.

## 2. Test mocks leak permanently into the process-global agent registry

I confirmed this with a probe test. After the two new tests run, `agent.StringList()` still contains `ext-available-test` and `ext-installed-test` for the remainder of the package run:

```
registry after external tests: claude-code,codex,copilot-cli,cursor,
  ext-available-test,ext-installed-test,factoryai-droid,gemini,opencode,pi,roger-roger
```

There is no `Unregister` in `agent/registry.go`. Their binaries live in `t.TempDir()`s that are deleted at test end, so every later `GetAgentsWithHooksInstalled` call in the package attempts to exec a deleted path. It's benign *today* only because a missing binary reports `installed: false` — that's TempDir cleanup ordering doing the isolation work, not the test. Had the mock reporting `{"installed": true}` outlived its directory, it would have polluted the installed-agent set package-wide.

Worth an `agent.UnregisterForTesting` (or snapshot/restore) seam wired to `t.Cleanup`. The full suite passes as-is, so this is hygiene, not a live failure.

## Smaller notes

- **`agent list --all` silently omits plugins whose `info` fails.** Verified: a plugin exiting non-zero is simply absent, exit 0, no diagnostic — while `agent add <same>` reports the underlying error fine. `docs/architecture/external-agent-protocol.md:553` documents skip-on-failure as protocol behavior, so this is by design, but `--all` is an explicit "what's on my PATH" inventory request where a one-line stderr warning would save real debugging time.
- **Doubled prefix in the error chain:** `... from binary "...": info: info: boom: cannot start`. Pre-existing wrap in the `external` package, but this PR is what first surfaces it to users.
- **No hint that `--all` exists.** The default listing gives no pointer. Repo convention (`entire investigate --findings` printing `view: entire investigate show <run-id>`) suggests a footer line.
- **`--all` bypasses the `external_agents` gate**, executing plugins for a user who never opted in. Defensible — the flag is the opt-in and the binaries are prefix-scoped to `entire-agent-*` — just confirming it's intentional.
- **CLAUDE.md:54** lists `agent`'s subcommands without the new `--all` flag. `agent-help` renders live from Cobra, so that surface updates itself.

Tests correctly avoid `t.Parallel()` alongside `t.Chdir`/`t.Setenv` and document why, matching the repo's guidance. The `sh`-availability skip matches sibling tests.

## Install vs upgrade

Rather than gate client-side, the event fires on every install and upgrade and the split is derived downstream — the standard telemetry pattern (this is how Homebrew's own analytics work):

- **`distinct_id`** is the hashed per-machine id, so PostHog's first-touch = install, repeats = upgrades.
- **`previous_version`** is read from a small persisted `install_state.json` in the **config** dir (empty on first install), giving an explicit, cache-clear-proof upgrade signal and version-transition history.

# Review: PR #1932 — `feat: track CLI installs to PostHog (curl / brew / scoop)`

**Author:** gtrrz-victor · `install-tracking-posthog` → `main` · +271/−7 across 9 files · OPEN

**Verification:** checked out the PR head (`175d40d19`) in a worktree. `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/telemetry/... ./cmd/entire/cli/versioncheck/...` green · `mise run lint` 0 issues · `bash -n scripts/install.sh` clean · shellcheck clean.

## Overview

Adds a `cli_installed` PostHog event fired from the three distribution channels, reusing the existing detached-spawn pipeline. The design is sound: no second PostHog client, `machineid.ProtectedID` for distinct_id consistent with existing events, a closed method allowlist, and `previous_version` persisted in the config dir (not the cache) so upgrade signal survives a cache wipe. Exporting `versioncheck.ReleaseChannel` is a clean reuse rather than a reimplementation. The opt-out check matches the `!= ""` convention used at all five existing sites.

## Answering your open question

**Nothing needs wiring in `.goreleaser.nonprod.yaml` — it publishes no cask or scoop manifest.** Its top-level keys are `builds`, `archives`, `blobs`, `release`, with `release: disable: true` and blobs going to an S3 bucket under `commit/{{.FullCommit}}`. There is no `homebrew_casks` and no `scoops` section, so there is no post-install hook to attach and no user-facing install path that could emit. Nightly casks come from the *prod* config via `skip_upload: "{{ if not .Prerelease }}true{{ end }}"` on the `entire@nightly` cask, which your diff does cover. I'd close the question as "intended, nothing to do".

## Findings

### 1. The brew hook is unguarded against the exact failure you flagged as unverifiable — Medium

Scoop gets `try { … } catch { }`; brew gets a bare `system_command`. That asymmetry matters more than it looks:

```ruby
system_command "#{staged_path}/entire", args: ["__track-install", "--method", "brew"]
```

I checked Homebrew's source (`Library/Homebrew/system_command.rb:44,102`) — `system_command` defaults to `must_succeed: false`, so a **non-zero exit** is safely ignored. But a **missing or non-executable** `#{staged_path}/entire` raises `Errno::ENOENT` from Ruby, which is not a non-zero exit and is not swallowed — it aborts `brew install`. That is precisely the case you called out as untestable in CI, on the highest-traffic channel, with no guard.

Suggest making brew as defensive as scoop:

```ruby
begin
  system_command "#{staged_path}/entire", args: ["__track-install", "--method", "brew"], must_succeed: false
rescue => e
  opoo "install tracking skipped: #{e}"
end
```

Worth noting the Gatekeeper angle is *not* a problem here — `.goreleaser.yaml:56` notarizes both darwin build ids with `wait: true`, so a quarantined-binary kill isn't in play.

### 2. A documented privacy guarantee rests on two unsynchronized string literals with no test — Medium

`docs/security-and-privacy.md` commits to an exact property set for this pre-consent event. Enforcement is:

- `detached.go:259` — `Event: "cli_installed"` (the producer)
- `detached.go:200` — `if payload.Event != "cli_installed"` (the suppressor, in the **detached child**)

`grep -rn '"cli_installed"'` finds only these two plus one test assertion, and no test exercises the suppression — `grep -rn git_version cmd/entire/cli/telemetry/` returns only the implementation. Rename the event in one place and the child silently starts attaching `git_version` to a pre-consent event whose disclosure says it has none.

The other event names in this package are also bare literals, so this isn't a convention break — the difference is that this one has a *second, remote consumer enforcing a privacy property*. Suggest a package const plus extracting the enrichment into a testable helper, since `SendEvent` currently has no seam (it constructs a real PostHog client inline):

```go
const eventCLIInstalled = "cli_installed"

func enrichProperties(p *EventPayload) { … }  // testable; assert no git_version for eventCLIInstalled
```

### 3. `previous_version` advances even when the event never ships — Low

`TrackInstallDetached` calls `writeInstalledVersion(version)` before `spawnDetachedAnalytics`, and the spawn is silently best-effort (`execx.SpawnDetached` returns early on `os.Executable()` or `cmd.Start()` failure). The comment covers the converse — "a write failure must never drop the event" — but not this direction: a dropped event still burns the version transition, so the next upgrade reports a `previous_version` whose install was never recorded. Moving the write after a successful `cmd.Start()` would need a return value from `SpawnDetached`; alternatively just note it as accepted loss.

Related, for whoever builds the dashboard: re-running `curl | bash` on the same version emits `previous_version == cli_version`. That's a reinstall, not an upgrade, and downstream needs to treat it as such.

### 4. Minor

- **`writeInstalledVersion` bypasses `installStatePath()`** (`detached.go:330`), re-joining `"install_state.json"` inline while `readInstalledVersion` uses the helper. Two places to change the filename. Given the repo's `dupl` linter culture, worth tightening.
- **Trailing redundant `return`** in `writeInstalledVersion`'s final `if err := os.WriteFile(...); err != nil { return }` — the function ends there anyway.
- **Hidden-command naming drift**: `__send_analytics` (underscore) vs `__track-install` (hyphen), adjacent in `root.go`. Cosmetic, but they're four lines apart.
- **`TestTrackInstallCmd_RequiresMethod`** calls `cmd.Execute()` without `SetOut`/`SetErr`, so cobra's usage output lands on the real stderr and pollutes test logs.

## Things I checked that are fine

- **Test safety** — `execx.SpawnDetached` early-returns under `testing.Testing()`, so no test can emit a real event. `TestInstalledVersionRoundTrip` correctly sets `ENTIRE_CONFIG_DIR` and skips `t.Parallel()`; the `userdirs` in-process fallback covers the tests that don't.
- **Scoop's `try/catch`** is right for the case that matters — a native exe's non-zero exit doesn't throw in PowerShell, but a missing `$dir\entire.exe` does, which is what the guard catches.
- **`install.sh` placement** before the PATH early-exit is correct, and `|| true` plus the detached spawn keeps it non-blocking. Env vars set ahead of `curl … | bash` do reach the child.
- **Opt-out consistency** — `!= ""` matches all five existing call sites, so `ENTIRE_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=0` opting *out* is pre-existing behavior, not something this PR introduces.

## One judgment call for you, not a defect

Brew and scoop users get **no install-time disclosure at all** — the hook fires silently, and the only notice lives in `docs/security-and-privacy.md`. `install.sh` at least prints a line, though it prints and pings in the same breath, so it informs rather than offers a choice. Given this is pre-consent and keyed to a pseudonymous per-machine ID, that's a product/legal call rather than a code one. It's mitigated by the EU PostHog endpoint (`eu.i.posthog.com`) and `DisableGeoIP`, and the payload is genuinely minimal. Flagging it so the decision is explicit rather than implicit — you may want whoever owns privacy sign-off to confirm the brew/scoop silence is acceptable before this ships.

# Homebrew Analytics Overview

## What's Collected

Homebrew gathers aggregate, anonymous usage data including:
- Package names and GitHub tap identifiers
- Installation options and dependency context
- System details (CPU architecture, OS, Homebrew version)
- Command names and options (with values removed)
- Build error information (without logs or exception details)

The payload explicitly excludes user identifiers and IP addresses.

## Opt-In or Opt-Out?

**Opt-out model.** The documentation states: "Homebrew displays a notice before analytics are enabled so a user can opt out before sending an event." However, the specific disclosure mechanism (e.g., first-run message text) is not detailed in this document.

## Disabling Analytics

Users can opt out using:
```
brew analytics off
```

Or set the environment variable:
```
export HOMEBREW_NO_ANALYTICS=1
```

## Formula/Cask-Level Tracking

Yes, analytics track individual formulas and casks. The data helps maintainers "prioritise widely used formulae, casks, commands and supported platforms" and identify "where installation or build failures are concentrated."

## Data Retention

"Homebrew retains analytics events in InfluxDB for 365 days."

require "cask/artifact/abstract_artifact"

module Cask
  module Artifact
    # Abstract superclass for block artifacts.
    class AbstractFlightBlock < AbstractArtifact
      sig { override.returns(Symbol) }
      def self.dsl_key
        super.to_s.sub(/_block$/, "").to_sym
      end

      sig { returns(Symbol) }
      def self.uninstall_dsl_key
        :"uninstall_#{dsl_key}"
      end

      sig { returns(T::Hash[Symbol, DirectivesType]) }
      attr_reader :directives

      sig { params(cask: Cask, directives: DirectivesType).void }
      def initialize(cask, **directives)
        super(cask)
        @directives = directives
      end

      sig { params(_options: T.anything).void }
      def install_phase(**_options)
        abstract_phase(self.class.dsl_key)
      end

      sig { params(_options: T.anything).void }
      def uninstall_phase(**_options)
        abstract_phase(self.class.uninstall_dsl_key)
      end

      sig { override.returns(String) }
      def summarize
        directives.keys.join(", ")
      end

      private

      sig { params(dsl_key: Symbol).returns(T::Class[::Cask::DSL::Base]) }
      def class_for_dsl_key(dsl_key)
        namespace = self.class.name.to_s.sub(/::.*::.*$/, "")
        # The DSL class name is derived dynamically from the flight block's key.
        # rubocop:disable Sorbet/ConstantsFromStrings
        self.class.const_get("#{namespace}::DSL::#{dsl_key.to_s.split("_").map(&:capitalize).join}")

      end

      sig { params(dsl_key: Symbol).void }
      def abstract_phase(dsl_key)
        return if (block = directives[dsl_key]).nil?

        class_for_dsl_key(dsl_key).new(cask).instance_eval(&T.cast(block, T.proc.returns(T.anything)))
      end
    end
  end

content.text:
Yes — and checking the precedent turned up something that changes one of my earlier findings.

## Correction to my review: the brew hook is riskier than I said

I previously said Homebrew's `system_command` defaults to `must_succeed: false` and so a non-zero exit is safely ignored. That's true of `SystemCommand.run`, but **the cask DSL doesn't call `run`** — `Cask::DSL::Base#system_command` (`cask/dsl/base.rb:28`) delegates to `@command.run!`, and `run!` defaults to `must_succeed: true` (`system_command.rb:129`).

So inside a cask hook, **any non-zero exit from `entire __track-install` raises and aborts `brew install`** — not just a missing binary. Finding #1 goes from Medium to High, and `must_succeed: false` moves from "nice to be explicit" to required. Good news from the same read: `staged_path` is a real delegator (`base.rb:25`), so `#{staged_path}/entire` resolves — the thing the author flagged as unverifiable is actually fine; it's the failure handling that isn't.

## Precedent in homebrew-cask

| Query | Result |
|---|---|
| Casks using `postflight` | 83 |
| Casks matching `analytics` + `postflight` | **0** |
| Casks matching `curl` + `postflight` | **0** |
| Casks matching `telemetry` | 8 — all app names/descriptions (VSCodium, Tableau, openusage), none a post-install ping |

I sampled the postflight bodies of ngrok, multipass, tidelift, orbstack. All are local setup — `set_permissions`, `symlink`, or invoking the app's own binary for local configuration. **No cask in the official repo phones home from postflight.**

The closest structural precedent is OrbStack:

```ruby
postflight_steps do
  run "OrbStack.app/Contents/MacOS/bin/orbctl", args: ["_internal", "brew-postflight"], base: :appdir
end
```

Same shape as this PR — a hidden vendor subcommand called from postflight. I can't tell from the cask what `orbctl _internal brew-postflight` does; the naming suggests local setup, not analytics. Note it uses the modern declarative `postflight_steps`, which per the Cask Cookbook runs sandboxed **without network access** — so that form couldn't do what this PR wants even if OrbStack wanted to. GoReleaser's `hooks:` emits the legacy `postflight do … end` block instead, which `instance_eval`s arbitrary Ruby unsandboxed (`cask/artifact/abstract_flight_block.rb`). That path still works, but it's the deprecated one, and it's deprecated precisely because arbitrary install-time code is what Homebrew is moving away from.

Third-party taps aren't bound by homebrew-cask policy, and I found no written Homebrew rule against this — Acceptable-Casks doesn't mention telemetry at all. So this isn't prohibited. It's just genuinely unusual.

## Comparable CLIs

The dev-tool CLIs I could inspect directly don't do it. Graphite (`withgraphite/tap`) ships a plain formula with no `post_install` — and Graphite definitely has telemetry, it just collects at runtime. Bun's formula likewise. GitHub code search for goreleaser configs wiring analytics into cask/scoop post-install returned one unrelated hit.

## One thing that argues *for* the PR

I checked whether Homebrew's own analytics could give you this for free. They can't: `formulae.brew.sh/api/analytics/cask-install/30d.json` covers 11,405 casks from homebrew-cask only, and `entire` isn't in it. Homebrew collects tap-identified events but doesn't publish third-party tap data, and `brew info --analytics entireio/tap/entire` returns nothing. So there is no off-the-shelf source for your brew install counts — the gap the PR is filling is real.

## One thing that argues against the current shape

The PR body cites Homebrew's own analytics as the model. That precedent cuts the other way on disclosure: per [docs.brew.sh/Analytics](https://docs.brew.sh/Analytics), "Homebrew displays a notice before analytics are enabled so a user can opt out **before sending an event**." Homebrew is opt-out *with* a pre-send notice. This PR's brew and scoop paths send with no notice at all — only `install.sh` prints anything, and it prints and pings in the same breath. If you're invoking the Homebrew precedent, the matching behavior would be a first-run notice before the first event, not a docs-only disclosure.

**Net:** the mechanism has precedent (OrbStack-shaped), the goal is legitimate (no free alternative exists for third-party taps), but zero casks in the official corpus phone home from postflight, and the `run!` discovery means the current hook can break `brew install` outright. I'd fix the `must_succeed` issue regardless of how the disclosure question lands.

Sources: [Homebrew Analytics](https://docs.brew.sh/Analytics), [Cask Cookbook](https://docs.brew.sh/Cask-Cookbook), [Acceptable Casks](https://docs.brew.sh/Acceptable-Casks), [GoReleaser homebrew_casks](https://goreleaser.com/customization/homebrew_casks/)

```ruby
hooks:

      begin
        system_command "#{staged_path}/entire",
                       args: ["__track-install", "--method", "brew"],
                       must_succeed: false
      rescue => e
        opoo "install tracking skipped: #{e}"
      end
```
